problem: Existing CATE estimation methods perform poorly in low-overlap regions where treatment propensity scores are extreme.
approach: Overlap-Adaptive Regularization (OAR) regularizes target models proportionally to overlap weights, increasing regularization strength in low-overlap regions and preserving Neyman-orthogonality for robust inference.
contribution: OAR significantly improves CATE estimation in low-overlap settings compared to constant regularization across both parametric and non-parametric meta-learners.

problem: Individualized differential privacy causes utility imbalance: data from owners with stronger privacy requirements becomes underrepresented in trained models, degrading performance on sensitive subgroups.
approach: INO-SGD strategically down-weights data within batches to improve performance on more private data while satisfying individualized privacy constraints.
contribution: INO-SGD is the first algorithm designed to address utility imbalance while satisfying individualized differential privacy guarantees.

problem: Existing universal prediction bounds for stochastic sequences hold only in expectation, not with high probability guarantees.
approach: Derives high-probability regret bounds for universal prediction over countable alphabets with convergence rate O(T^-1/2 δ^-1/2), complementing prior expectation-based bounds.
contribution: Establishes vanishing high-probability regret bounds with similar form to prior expectation bounds and proves an impossibility result on improving the δ exponent.

problem: LLMs suffer performance degradation on long contexts due to proactive interference from irrelevant information disrupting reasoning and memory.
approach: Sculptor equips LLMs with Active Context Management tools including context fragmentation, summarization, and precise search to sculpt internal working memory, plus dynamic context-aware RL training.
contribution: Sculptor significantly improves performance on long-context benchmarks without specific training and mitigates proactive interference through explicit context-control strategies.

problem: Image-guided multimodal translation is constrained by scarcity of multilingual image-text pairs, limiting language coverage.
approach: Speech-guided Multimodal Machine Translation (SMMT) uses speech and text fusion in an MLLM with a Self-Evolution Mechanism to synthesize speech and iteratively optimize using positive samples.
contribution: SMMT achieves state-of-the-art on Multi30K and new state-of-the-art average performance on FLORES-200 across 108 translation directions.

problem: Graph similarity measures often rely on costly transportation-based metrics; efficient approximations enabling graph retrieval at scale are lacking.
approach: Discovers exchangeability property in GNN embeddings enabling approximation of transportation-based graph similarities via Euclidean distances between order statistics and proposes unified locality-sensitive hashing framework.
contribution: LSH framework supports diverse relevance measures including subgraph matching and graph edit distance more effectively than baselines.

problem: LLM agents can be tricked into executing harmful goals decomposed into benign subtasks; shallow alignment techniques fail to reason about long-range intent.
approach: Proposes lightweight sequential monitoring framework observing conversation at higher level, curates DecomposedHarm dataset with 4,634 tasks, and uses prompt-engineered monitors with cumulative sub-prompt evaluation.
contribution: Lightweight sequential monitors achieve 93% defense success rate against decomposition attacks while cutting costs by 90% and latency by 50%.

problem: Multimodal alignment post-training leaves user role unaligned and assumes fixed input prompt structure, making VLMs vulnerable to structural perturbations.
approach: Introduces Role-Modality Attacks (RMA) exploiting role confusion and image token position changes, and proposes adversarial training using perturbed prompts to achieve robustness.
contribution: Adversarial training makes VLMs robust to input prompt perturbations with substantial Attack Success Rate reduction.

problem: Diffusion models reproduce exact training images; existing norm-based memorization detection assumes isotropic log-probability distributions which fails in low-noise anisotropic regime.
approach: Develops memorization detection metric integrating isotropic norm and anisotropic alignment (angular alignment between guidance vector and unconditional scores) computed via two forward passes.
contribution: Detection metric outperforms existing denoising-free methods and is approximately 5x faster than prior best approach.

problem: Optical flow methods rely on cost volumes which are computationally expensive; simpler warping-based approaches are unexplored.
approach: WAFT replaces cost volume with high-resolution warping, using a simple flexible meta-architecture with minimal inductive biases.
contribution: WAFT ranks 1st on Spring, Sintel, and KITTI benchmarks, achieves best zero-shot generalization on KITTI, and is up to 4.1x faster than similar-performance methods.

problem: Linear attention mechanisms show improvement but decay matrix design is structurally limited to Diagonal-Plus-Rank-1, restricting expressiveness.
approach: HDLA uses efficient matrix decomposition to achieve Diagonal-Plus-Rank-2 decay structure and proposes chunk-wise parallel algorithm accommodating diagonal-plus-rank-r decay and key-value outer products.
contribution: HDLA sets new SOTA on language modeling and retrieval at 2.8B scale, with up to 80% performance gains on retrieval tasks.

problem: Existing LLM evaluation benchmarks are prone to saturation and memorization or rely on subjective comparisons; assessing LLM capability for combinatorial optimization is underexplored.
approach: HeuriGym is an agentic framework where LLMs propose heuristics, receive code-execution feedback, and iteratively refine solutions, with Quality-Yield Index metric capturing solution pass rate and quality.
contribution: Evaluation of nine SOTA models reveals persistent limitations; even GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-2.5-Pro achieve only 0.6 QYI compared to expert baseline of 1.

problem: LLMs exhibit cultural bias and limited awareness of underrepresented cultures; mechanisms underlying cultural understanding remain unexplored.
approach: Identifies culture-general and culture-specific neurons via gradient-based scoring, showing they account for <1% of neurons and concentrate in shallow-to-middle MLP layers.
contribution: Suppressing culture-specific neurons degrads cultural benchmark performance by up to 30% with minimal impact on general NLU, revealing cultural knowledge mechanisms.

problem: Decentralized composite optimization over networks without central coordinators suffers from communication bottlenecks limiting scalability.
approach: Proposes decentralized Symmetric ADMM incorporating multiple communication rounds per iteration with new constraint formulation enabling beyond-neighbor information exchange and optimal communication rules.
contribution: Achieves linear convergence while reducing total iterations and overall communication cost compared to existing decentralized methods.

problem: Existing motion-language models face quantization errors capping motion quality and cross-modal interference when unifying discrete text and continuous motion in single-stream architecture.
approach: MotionGPT3 encodes raw motion into continuous latent space via VAE and uses dual-stream Transformer with shared attention to preserve modality-specific routes while enabling controlled bidirectional flow.
contribution: Achieves 2x faster training convergence in loss and up to 4x faster validation convergence while maintaining SOTA performance on motion understanding and generation.

problem: Training GUI agents is limited by reliance on unsafe live web interactions or expensive scarce human-crafted data; efficiently compressing LLM knowledge into agent behavior is underexplored.
approach: WebFactory automates closed-loop RL pipeline: environment synthesis -> knowledge-aware task generation -> LLM trajectory collection -> decomposed reward RL training -> agent evaluation.
contribution: Agent trained on synthetic data from 10 websites achieves performance comparable to agents trained on same human-annotated data from much larger environments.

problem: Omni-modal LLMs aim for modality-invariant reasoning but whether they achieve it or inherit modality-specific biases is unclear.
approach: XModBench is a 60K-question tri-modal benchmark with five task families covering all six cross-modality directions to measure cross-modal consistency and diagnose task competence and modality disparity.
contribution: Even Gemini-2.5-Pro struggles with spatial/temporal reasoning (<60% accuracy) and exhibits 20+ point modality disparities and directional imbalance.

problem: Classical predictive coding formulations are unidirectional (generative or discriminative) but experimental evidence suggests brains employ bidirectional processing.
approach: Proposes bidirectional PC (bPC) combining generative and discriminative inference via energy landscape simultaneously supporting both tasks with biologically plausible circuit implementation.
contribution: bPC matches or outperforms unidirectional models on specialized tasks and shows superior performance on multimodal learning and inference with missing information.

problem: Pixel-space generative models train poorly and underperform latent-space counterparts; persistent performance and efficiency gaps limit adoption.
approach: Two-stage framework: pre-train encoders capturing semantics from clean images aligned with deterministic sampling trajectory points, then fine-tune end-to-end for diffusion and consistency models.
contribution: Pixel-space diffusion achieves FID 1.58 on ImageNet-256 and 2.35 on ImageNet-512, surpassing VAE counterparts with only ~30% of DiT training compute; consistency model achieves FID 8.82 on ImageNet-256.

problem: Class incremental learning with only unlabeled data and class names is realistic but pseudo-label noise aggravates catastrophic forgetting.
approach: N2L uses regression with MSE loss solved recursively, applies feature dimensionality reduction, and iteratively updates labels using reduced-feature classifier with bi-level weight adjustment for confidence and class imbalance.
contribution: Achieves performance equivalent to joint training with unlabeled data, mitigating catastrophic forgetting and outperforming SOTA methods.

problem: SAM2 shows excellent video segmentation but heavy computational burden hinders real-time video processing; post-training acceleration is underexplored.
approach: Proposes object-aware Sparse Window Routing (SWR) for image encoder and Sparse Memory Retrieval (SMR) for memory attention to eliminate redundant background computation leveraging consistency and saliency cues.
contribution: Efficient-SAM2 significantly improves inference efficiency by adaptively focusing on object regions.

problem: Existing safety fine-tuning for VLMs lacks visual reasoning ability in safety-critical contexts; multi-image safety scenarios are underexplored.
approach: Introduces Multi-Image Safety (MIS) dataset with multi-image inputs and safety Chain-of-Thought labels for fine-grained reasoning logic.
contribution: Fine-tuning InternVL2.5-8B with MIS increases accuracy by 0.83% on general benchmarks and substantially reduces Attack Success Rate on safety benchmarks.

problem: Pose-based human animation relies on error-prone pose estimators sensitive to occlusion and complex poses.
approach: DirectAnimator bypasses pose extraction using Driving Cue Triplet (pose, face, location) fused via CueFusion DiT, with Same2X training strategy aligning cross-ID features with same-ID data.
contribution: Achieves SOTA visual quality and identity preservation while remaining robust to occlusions and complex articulation with fewer resources.

problem: Web agents struggle with short-horizon subtasks on UI components; existing benchmarks do not extensively evaluate subtask mastery.
approach: WARC-Bench features 438 tasks on dynamic webpages via Web ARChive files, evaluated via SFT and RL with verifiable rewards.
contribution: SFT achieves 48.8% success rate; RLVR over SFT improves to 52.8%, outperforming many frontier models on critical web navigation subtasks.

problem: How LLM performance evolves during self-improvement training remains underexplored despite self-improvement being a significant technique.
approach: Theoretically models self-improvement dynamics via solver-verifier gap concept; shows how to model entire training trajectory and quantify capability limits by fitting to experiments.
contribution: Framework validated on various LLMs and datasets reveals that external data can be utilized at any stage in limited-data regimes without significantly affecting final performance.

problem: Traditional learning rate decay is computationally expensive during LLM pre-training; decay-free scheduling via model merging lacks theoretical foundation.
approach: WSM establishes formal connection between LR decay and model merging, unifying cosine/linear/inverse-sqrt decay as principled model averaging compatible with diverse optimizers.
contribution: Consistently outperforms Warmup-Stable-Decay with improvements of +3.5% MATH, +2.9% HumanEval, +5.5% MMLU-Pro.

problem: Fine-tuning open-source LLMs with proprietary data is standard practice but data owners can extract private fine-tuning data via backdoor training.
approach: Demonstrates backdoor extraction attack where open-source LLM provider can extract downstream fine-tuning data through simple training with black-box model access.
contribution: Extraction performance reaches 76.3% of 5,000 query samples in practical settings and up to 94.9% in ideal settings; defense strategies are ineffective.

problem: Contextual pricing under semi-parametric demand model with Hölder-continuous link function has suboptimal regret rates and requires restrictive assumptions.
approach: Combines stationary subroutine with local polynomial regression under unimodality condition, achieving unified rate O(T^((β+1)/(2β+1))) for all β≥1.
contribution: Recovers and strengthens existing results for β=1,2, removes derivative lower bound assumptions, and improves practical performance with reduced exploration phases.

problem: Multimodal LLM evaluation lacks assessment of cognitive capabilities like execution, perception reasoning, learning, memory, and planning that mirror children's development.
approach: KidGym is a 2D grid-based benchmark with 12 tasks inspired by Wechsler Intelligence Scales, with random object layouts and customizable difficulty levels.
contribution: Evaluation of SOTA MLLMs reveals significant limitations and provides actionable insights into model capabilities.

problem: Current foundation models capture either tissue context or sequence features but not both; alternative splicing and isoform reuse are overlooked.
approach: CDBridge is a post-training strategy unifying DNA and protein models via splicing-inspired token merge for isoform-aware representations and conditional decoder injecting tissue embeddings.
contribution: Consistently outperforms prior methods on GTEx-Benchmark, capturing long-range exon dependencies and resolving isoform reuse for tissue-specific expression prediction.

problem: Standard softmax attention with uncontrolled query/key norms causes training instabilities even on simple data with spurious patterns.
approach: QUEST constrains keys to hyperspherical latent space while allowing tokens to control attention sharpness via query-modulated spherical attention.
contribution: QUEST trains without instabilities and produces models with improved performance robust to data corruptions and adversarial attacks.

problem: Monocular RGB-based human performance capture lacks sufficient observations for unseen regions.
approach: Maintains progressively updated canonical space accumulating appearance over time and formulates rendering as probabilistic regression to resolve conflicts between past and current observations.
contribution: Produces sharper reconstructions than deterministic regression and enables plausible synthesis in regions with no prior observations.

problem: High-fidelity generative modeling of neuronal morphologies is underexplored but crucial for connectomics.
approach: MoGen uses flow matching to generate high-resolution 3D point clouds with local geometric context injected into scalable latent transformer backbone.
contribution: Augmenting connectomics pipeline training set with MoGen samples improves classifier accuracy and reduces split/merge errors by 4.4%, potentially reducing manual proofreading by over 157 person-years.

problem: Static task-specific LLM benchmarks are fragile to contamination and saturation; interactive evaluation capturing reasoning is lacking.
approach: Reframes evaluation as teaching: candidate model guides weaker students and student gains score the model via Application/Judgment/Guidance/Reflection metrics.
contribution: Achieves Spearman >0.95 with human-preference leaderboards, surpasses direct baselines, and provides actionable training signals.

problem: Existing mistake detection focuses on action execution but overlooks what actions produce, i.e., action effects; many errors manifest in resulting outcomes not execution.
approach: Action Effect Modeling (AEM) jointly captures execution and outcomes via probabilistic formulation, selecting informative effect frames and extracting complementary cues via visual grounding and scene graphs.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on EgoPER and CaptainCook4D under one-class classification setting by modeling both execution and outcome.

problem: Diffusion LLMs discard rich intermediate predictions during denoising despite temporal oscillation where correct answers emerge mid-process.
approach: Introduces Temporal Self-Consistency Voting (training-free test-time decoding aggregating predictions) and Temporal Consistency Reinforcement using Temporal Semantic Entropy as reward signal.
contribution: Achieves average improvement of 24.7% on Countdown and gains of 2.0% GSM8K, 4.3% MATH500, 6.6% SVAMP with temporal consistency methods.

problem: Structured image reasoning (charts, diagrams) fails in MLLMs due to perceptual slips cascading into erroneous conclusions.
approach: Multi-agent system with dispatcher, planner, reasoner, critics, and visual tool agents; fine-tunes MLLM into grounding model with pixel-level localization integrated with CV algorithms.
contribution: Dynamic three-stage workflow with image memory enables flexible reasoning, significantly improving visual reasoning on chart and geometry benchmarks.

problem: Open-source web agents significantly underperform proprietary systems; training scalable high-capability agents is challenging.
approach: Complete post-training pipeline with SailorFog-QA-2 dataset built from interconnected knowledge graph and dual-environment RL combining high-fidelity simulator with robust real-world environment.
contribution: Qwen3-30B-A3B agent achieves 35.3 BrowseComp-EN, 44.1 BrowseComp-ZH, 30.6 HLE, surpassing DeepSeek-V3.1 and competing with proprietary systems.

problem: Federated learning communication overhead is critical; existing compression methods rely on magnitude heuristics ignoring output discrepancy.
approach: Uses calibration data on clients to measure output discrepancy induced by dropping compression units as compression metric guiding selection.
contribution: Achieves 18.9% relative accuracy improvement at 0.1 compression ratio under severe communication constraints.

problem: Dynamic personalized summarization requires capturing time-variant subjective preferences but existing models assume memoryless or short-memory Markovian diffusion.
approach: Walk2Pers extends random walk view with action-conditioned geometric steps decomposed into magnitude and orientation mediated by dual memory lanes suppressing disinterest.
contribution: Outperforms specialized personalized summarizers by 0.41 PerSEval and strong LLM baselines by 0.22 with cross-domain robustness of 0.19 over best LLM.
